howDoI.q: How do I teach a new idea without frightening anyone?
How do I add a little danger to something I already taught?
How do I use the same idea in a way nobody expects?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Teach, Test, Twist is a Starter about the order a good level is made in. It has three tiny levels and one idea, a gap in the ground, and the idea comes back each time a little different. It takes a few minutes to finish.

  1. Teach. Show the idea where nothing can go wrong.
  2. Test. Ask for it again, with a little danger.
  3. Twist. Use the same idea in a new way, so the player feels clever.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and look at how each level is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: Teach
pages.html:
Level 1: Teach

The STEP 1, TEACH sign comes first and says what the room is about: a gap. Two blocks of ground are missing, and you can see across it. Jump over it. Then read the second sign, NOTHING HURTS HERE, and go back and drop in: there is a coin at the bottom, and you can walk out the other side. Nothing here can hurt you, so the first time the player meets the idea, they can try it any way they like.

Every way out is in plain sight, and the exit door has its own sign. Nothing is hidden: you can see what is dangerous and where to go next.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The gap. Open one.map in the map editor. The ground is grass over dirt. Take away the top two rows of ground for three blocks, and what is left at the bottom is a new floor of grass. A gap is only missing blocks.
  • Why it is safe. The floor is two blocks down, and Lena can jump two blocks (they jump a brick wall that tall in Your First Game), so there is always a way out. Check this when you make a gap of your own: can they get out of it?
  • The coin. It sits on the gap’s floor. It is a reward for trying the safe way, and the player who jumps over simply passes it.
  • The signs. A sign is a few ordinary blocks with words drawn on them. The first one names the step (teach), the second one says it is safe. Words on the screen teach better than a long page.

pages.head: Level 2: Test
pages.html:
Level 2: Test

The STEP 2, TEST sign says the same gap has spikes at the bottom now. You can see them, so nobody is tricked. Drop in, and the spikes sting (10 hit points each) and lie flat. Climb out and go on. A second, wider gap waits farther along. The RUN, THEN JUMP sign tells you what to do: take a few steps first and jump from the edge. A little danger asks the player to use what they learned, and a mistake costs a few hit points, not the game.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The same gap. Open two.map. The first gap is the same size as in level 1. The idea has not changed, only what is at the bottom.
  • The spikes. In ttt.bbl pick spikeUp. Its Hit points is −10 and Becomes block is spikeFlat, so a spike hurts once and then lies down. Lena starts with 50 hit points: open hero.chr and look at the first counter. The Watch Your Step Starter goes further.
  • A wider gap. Make the gap one block wider and the same jump now needs a run. Play after each change, and stop when it takes a good jump but not a perfect one.
  • Danger you can see. The spikes are drawn on the floor of the gap in plain sight. A player should be able to look at the screen and know what will hurt.

pages.head: Level 3: Twist
pages.html:
Level 3: Twist

The STEP 3, TWIST sign says NOW YOU WANT IN. The same gap is here, but this time the key to the locked door is at the bottom, so the player drops in on purpose and climbs out. Farther on, the wider spiked gap is back from level 2 and has to be jumped. Then the locked door opens with the key. The player already knows how to jump a gap and how to get out of one. The twist is that the gap went from being a problem to being the goal.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The key in the gap. Open three.map. The key is one block on the floor of a gap like the one from level 1. In ttt.bbl, key has an Effect counter of 20 and an Effect amount of 1.
  • The locked door. The gate block is solid. Its Effect counter is 20 too, with an Effect amount of −1, so the door only gives way with a key. The Keys and Doors Starter has the whole story.
  • No way around. The door is in a wall of brick that goes to the top of the level, so the key cannot be skipped.
  • Old pieces, new job. Everything in this level is a block from the first two, so nothing new has to be taught. A twist works best when it reuses what the player already knows.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

This game uses nothing new, and there are things the pattern cannot do for you:

  • Game-Maker cannot tell you whether a level teaches well. Play it with a friend and watch where they stop.
  • The engine has no check for the ground when you jump, so a player can jump in the air. Keep that in mind when you plan a gap.
  • A level cannot change on its own after the player learns something. The twist has to be built into the map.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Open the game with Edit a copy, so the original stays safe. Then make one change at a time, and play after each.

  1. Change the words. Open ttt.bbl in the blocks editor, pick a sign block (they are named like teach.sign) and change its words.
  2. Make the gap wider. In one.map take away more ground. Can Lena still jump it?
  3. Pick another idea. Instead of a gap, try a spring, a switch or a monster from another Starter. Make one level that teaches it safely, one that tests it, and one that twists it.
  4. Make the twist your own. What if the gap had a ladder? A coin you could only get from below? A door at the bottom?
